items: THINK/EXECUTE split: explore-diagnose-design-decide runs at hub or deep child and must end in a verdict+recipe; only known-change execution goes to quick/moderate children

Straight-line brief checklist on every execute dispatch: exact paths/symbols, exact change, verify commands, done-format, stop conditions; a brief that needs exploration means the thinking is not done yet
Verdict packet handback: deep children return structured verdict (decision, numbered exact recipe, evidence, open questions) instead of narrative; hub fans recipe out as execute briefs
No-improvise stop conditions for children: on assumption mismatch (file missing, state differs) return BLOCKED with the mismatch instead of improvising or widening scope
Wandering detection: if a child explores beyond its brief, stop it and fix/re-tier the brief rather than waiting it out (brief defect, not child defect)
question: Considering failure modes, second-order effects on token cost and latency, and how often each rule would fire in hub-and-spoke multi-agent workflows: how strongly does this rule prevent simple-tier subagents from wandering off a straight line?
